narrative.benchmark_md: The peers was locked in Batch 1 of the research phase and is immutable for this assessment. Five peers were selected based on sub-vertical match (SV1 Regional Banks), size tier proximity ($1B–$10B), geographic overlap (California-focused commercial banking), and competitive relevance: Bank of Marin Bancorp (BMRC), $3.7B, NorCal (60% overlap); Heritage Commerce Corp (HTBK), $5.0B, Bay Area (55% overlap); RBB Bancorp (RBB), $2.5B, LA/SoCal (85% overlap); Hanmi Financial (HAFC), $7.6B, LA/SoCal (70% overlap); and California BanCorp (BCAL), $2.8B, Oakland/California statewide (45% overlap). All peer scores are derived from public evidence and reflect category-level proxy assessments.
narrative.issue_register_md: Seven issues were identified and registered during the assessment research phase. Two MATERIAL issues impose binding level 3 score ceilings on specific capability clusters. Five MINOR issues impose level 4 ceilings. Together, 115 of 698 capability are subject to active issue caps. All issue determinations are grounded in evidence and documented in the Caps_Applied column of the assessment workbook.

per_pillar_md.P1:
P1 is CalPrivate Bank's second-strongest pillar, where formal governance infrastructure and community standing deliver measurable advantages over peers. The IT Governance and ESG scores both reflect genuine, documented capability — not inference. The development opportunity in Innovation is the principal gap between CalPrivate's current position and a true level 4 Advanced P1 posture.
: Digital Strategy & Vision Score 2.70 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.2 | level 3 Established
What We See: CEO Sowers (ex-Accenture banking efficiency, since Feb 2018) articulated a $5B+ asset growth strategy [E-0001] supported by Q4 2025 Chairman Isakow's naming of AI, digital capabilities, and core systems as investment priorities [E-0002]. Investor relations materials document a formal Technology & Innovation roadmap process, with Product Strategy Roadmaps as explicit inputs to a broader Technology Roadmap [E-0107]. Technology principles — documented in the IR deck — include: investment in technology as a competitive necessity, improved client experience, scalability for organic growth and M&A [E-0107]. The newly hired SVP Director of Strategic Initiatives (Daniel Chang) [E-0123] indicates strategic execution capacity is being built. capability scores cluster at 2.5–3.0, reflecting a documented strategy but with limited quantified outcome evidence at the capability level.
Why It Matters: The strategic intent at CalPrivate is well-documented and board-aligned. The Chairman's AI mandate [E-0002] means that technology investment proposals do not need to create demand — they need only demonstrate alignment with a pre-authorized strategic direction. This is a meaningful procurement environment advantage for Zennify. The gap between strategy articulation (3.0) and innovation capability ( = 2.05) is the primary P1 development area: the 'what' is defined; the systematic mechanism for testing, piloting, and scaling new capabilities is not yet formal.
Peer Context: score 2.70 vs peer median 2.50 (+0.20). HTBK (Heritage Commerce, Bay Area, Silicon Valley proximity) likely leads peers on strategy sophistication given tech-industry client base. CalPrivate matches on documented strategy; HTBK advantage may stem from more explicit digital transformation investment disclosures.
: IT Governance & Risk Score 3.03 / 5.0 | Peer: 3 | Gap: +0.03 | level 3 Established
What We See: The Technology & Innovation Board Committee is co-chaired by Leda Csanka — 36-year CIO/CTO career — and provides board-level oversight of the technology roadmap, governance, and budget [E-0093, E-0107]. The Information Technology Management Committee is a cross-functional internal body focused on cybersecurity, emerging security trends, and enterprise adoption [E-0107]. Board Director Kathy Lonowski (ex-FDIC San Francisco Regional Director, 350+ financial institutions, $1T AUM) provides dual regulatory and digital banking governance expertise [E-0095]. CTO Curtis Birkmann holds BCP/DR certifications and leads a portfolio of 100+ technology projects [E-0093]. subcaps score in the 3.0–3.5 range: Digital Governance Charter (3.5), Steering Committee (3.5), Decision Rights Framework (3.5).
Why It Matters: The dual-layer governance structure — T&I Board Committee plus IT Management Committee — provides both strategic authorization and operational oversight. This is the most institutionally mature aspect of CalPrivate's technology posture and directly enables the Zennify engagement: Leda Csanka and Kathy Lonowski provide the board-level credibility to evaluate and approve a Salesforce FSC transformation. Budget approval does not require creating a governance process — it requires presenting to an existing one. This is a significant sales cycle accelerant.
Peer Context: score 3.03 vs peer median 3.00 (+0.03). CalPrivate matches or slightly exceeds peers on governance. The dedicated T&I Board Committee is a differentiator: most $1B–$5B community banks lack board-level technology committees with external CIO/CTO expertise.
: Innovation & Fintech Score 2.05 / 5.0 | Peer: 2 | Gap: +0.05 | level 2 Developing
What We See: CalPrivate participates in three structured FinTech ecosystems: BankTech Ventures, BankTech Consortium, and JAM FINTOP [E-0112] — providing access to emerging community banking technology research and early-stage fintech relationships. Kyle Bailey as SVP Product Management, Origination Technology [E-0123] represents the confirmed 'Product Strategy & Innovation team' hire referenced in the IR deck [E-0107]. nCino deployment (Q1 2023) and D365 deployment (2022) represent technology-forward decisions within the peers. subcaps score at 2.0–2.5, reflecting ecosystem access without a confirmed formal innovation lab, stage-gate process, or internal hackathon cadence.
Why It Matters: is the primary P1 development area. BankTech Ventures and JAM FINTOP provide an external FinTech radar, but a structured internal innovation process — pilot criteria, success metrics, scale gates — is not confirmed in public disclosures. The Product Strategy & Innovation team hire [E-0123] is the mechanism through which this gap is being addressed. Zennify's technology roadmap (FSC + MuleSoft + Einstein) introduces the structured, Salesforce-native framework within which future FinTech pilots can be evaluated and deployed.
Peer Context: score 2.05 vs peer median 2.00 (+0.05). CalPrivate is at the peer median on innovation — this category is uniformly underdeveloped across SV1 $1B–$5B community banks, where innovation typically means vendor adoption rather than internal R&D.
: Culture & Change Management Score 2.46 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: -0.04 | level 2 Developing
What We See: Glassdoor and Indeed employee data reflects a collaborative, client-relationship-focused culture: 78% salary satisfaction, 75% recommend to a friend, interview experience rated EXCELLENT [E-0012]. Six C-level and SVP hires in 12 months (COO, CCO, DCBO, SVP Credit Risk Analytics, Director Portfolio Management, SBA BDO) reflect aggressive organizational scaling [E-0019, E-0085] — an ISS-006 MINOR issue applying an level 4 ceiling. CEO Sowers' Q1 2026 statement emphasizes 'team strength' [E-0119] and the culture of Relationships, Solutions, and Trust is reinforced across public communications. subcaps score in the 2.0–2.5 range.
Why It Matters: The talent scaling risk (ISS-006) is not a culture failure — it is a growth management challenge. Six senior hires in 12 months doubles CalPrivate's C-suite density at exactly the point when the bank is formalizing its operational transformation agenda. COO Pierron's stated goal — 'build on the foundation, service our clients with excellence, and drive continued growth and innovation' [E-0085] — positions the new leadership cohort as additive rather than corrective. The Zennify deployment accelerates cultural alignment by systematizing workflows before new hires onboard into fragmented manual processes.
Peer Context: score 2.46 vs peer median 2.50 (−0.04). At peer median. Culture and change management is uniformly developing across the SV1 cohort — most community banks lack formal change management frameworks; change occurs through leadership relationship rather than process.
: ESG & Community Score 2.96 / 5.0 | Peer: 2 | Gap: +0.96 | level 3 Established
What We See: FDIC CRA examination: High Satisfactory across all three tests (Lending, Investment, Services), rated under Large Institution CRA examination procedures — the highest applicable rating for CalPrivate's size class [E-0090]. CalPrivate holds SBA Preferred Lender status; Community Bank SBA 504 Lender of the Year (NADCO Community Impact Awards); Bank Director's #1 bank in its asset class for ROA and ROE [E-0124]. American Banker top 5% of US banks with $2B–$10B assets for both 2024 and 2025 [E-0124]. Board member George Leis served as YMCA Chairman of the Board; 8+ named community partnerships documented in research [E-0034]. Bauer Financial 5-star rated. New Montecito branch opens with dedicated nonprofit Impact Checking account [E-0114].
Why It Matters: ESG & Community is CalPrivate's strongest peer-differentiated category — +0.96 above the SV1 the peer benchmark, the single largest positive gap in the entire 17-category assessment. The CRA High Satisfactory under Large Institution procedures is significant: it means CalPrivate is evaluated under the same rigor applied to banks many times its size. This compliance depth is a market differentiator in HNW relationship banking: clients and referring RIAs prioritize institutional credibility. Every Salesforce recommendation in this report operates from the foundation of a bank with no enforcement actions [E-0024] and the highest applicable CRA rating.
Peer Context: score 2.96 vs peer median 2.00 (+0.96). CalPrivate significantly outperforms all five peers on ESG. HAFC ($7.6B) has broader community investment capacity; CalPrivate leads on qualitative CRA outcomes and formal recognition. This is the most differentiated capability in the assessment.
per_pillar_md.P2:
P2 is the most strategically significant pillar in this assessment. The highest peer-relative strength ( Personalization, +0.68) and the most consequential development area ( Digital Onboarding, −0.48) both reside here. The tension is acute: CalPrivate delivers world-class client outcomes through relationship manager excellence while the digital infrastructure that would systematize and scale that excellence is underdeveloped. The Zennify engagement addresses this tension directly.
: Digital Marketing & Acquisition Score 2.43 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: -0.07 | level 2 Developing
What We See: Storm Brain digital agency confirmed as CalPrivate's primary digital marketing partner, having 'tripled email and social engagement' [E-0060]. LinkedIn presence: 2,987 followers with regular commercial banking content. Google Tag Manager and LinkedIn Insight Tag deployed for web analytics [E-0121]. SBA content marketing active (rates, eligibility, program descriptions). 19 demo videos documented on website for product education. GTM Analytics tracking confirmed. Testimonial content from named clients supports referral-based acquisition model [E-0073]. subcaps score in the 1.5–3.0 range: digital channel strategy and compliance-in-marketing strong; marketing automation scores 1.5 (no MA platform confirmed).
Why It Matters: Marketing Cloud is the category-level gap: Storm Brain tripled engagement, but the absence of a marketing automation platform means campaigns are agency-dependent and cannot be triggered by Salesforce data events. The connection between CFR data (which commercial client just closed a loan) and marketing activation (send treasury cross-sell journey) requires Marketing Cloud. The COO's seven years of EVP Head of Payments expertise [E-0119] is directly relevant: payments and treasury cross-sell are the highest-value campaigns for a commercial bank, and they require real-time data triggers, not scheduled agency campaigns.
Peer Context: score 2.43 vs peer median 2.50 (−0.07). Near parity. SoCal community banks at this tier all rely on agency-based digital marketing. CalPrivate's Storm Brain engagement results give it a slight quality advantage; the automation platform gap is shared across the cohort.
: Digital Onboarding & Fulfillment Score 2.02 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: -0.48 | level 2 Developing
What We See: IFS Banking confirmed as CalPrivate's digital banking and mobile platform [E-0050]. App Store reviews rate the IFS app as 'outdated, lacks basic functions' (ISS-003 MINOR cap). Business clients require a separate FIS Deposit One application for remote deposit capture [E-0085]. Digital Account Platform (DAP) announced in the 2023 Annual Report but current activation status not confirmed [E-0113]. SBA loan eligibility transparency strong: minimum FICO 650 published, government-guaranteed programs documented [E-0058]. nCino (Salesforce-native, Q1 2023) handles commercial lending origination with known-fast decisioning (SBA approvals documented) [E-0105]. capability range: 1.5–3.0. Strongest capability: Eligibility Transparency (3.0); weakest cluster: digital account opening subcaps (1.5–2.0).
Why It Matters: = 2.02 — the weakest of all 17 assessed categories and the single largest negative gap versus peers (−0.48). This is the most actionable finding in the P2 pillar. The bank's IFS app fragmentation, absent native digital account opening, and dual-app friction directly contradict the 'Distinctly Different™' experience promise at the digital channel. NPS 81 survives this gap because RM-led relationships compensate — but at $5B scale, the compensation model fails. nCino Deposit Account Opening (R-004) directly addresses the digital account opening gap: as nCino is already live and the DCBO SME role is posted [E-0086], the expansion path requires internal resource rather than a net-new vendor procurement.
Peer Context: score 2.02 vs peer median 2.50 (−0.48). This is the only material negative peer gap in the assessment. HAFC (Hanmi, $7.6B, NASDAQ-listed) leads the cohort on digital onboarding with a more mature mobile-first platform investment at its larger scale. RBB Bancorp, similar in size to CalPrivate, is estimated at 2.0-2.5 — the negative gap is therefore driven by IFS app age and the missing digital account opening capability.
: Omnichannel Servicing Score 2.52 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.02 | level 3 Established
What We See: CalPrivate operates three dedicated phone lines for retail, business, and Private Business Capital clients respectively, with M–F 9am–5pm banking hours (ISS-007 MINOR cap on ) [E-0067]. Secure Messaging is available through the IFS Banking platform for authenticated communication [E-0069]. Knowledge Center self-service resource library confirmed on the website [E-0068]. Can Truong: VP-Digital Banking & Operations Support Manager since 2015 confirms internal digital banking operations function [E-0123]. VoC and service performance subcaps score highest at 3.5 — driven by NPS 81 World Class ×15 consecutive quarters [E-0073]. Agent Enablement capped level 3 (ISS-002: D365+nCino+Excel fragmentation). Self-service subcaps capped level 4 (ISS-003: IFS app fragmentation).
Why It Matters: The NPS 81 outcome at is the strongest single capability signal in Pillar 2. It confirms that the RM-led servicing model delivers objectively superior client outcomes. The architectural challenge is that this excellence is not systematized: it resides in individual RM knowledge and relationship continuity. Service Cloud converts RM excellence from a human-dependent attribute into a platform-supported capability — case queues, SLAs, interaction history, and cross-branch visibility all contribute to making the NPS 81 model reproducible at scale and across 8+ branches.
Peer Context: score 2.52 vs peer median 2.50 (+0.02). At peer median. CalPrivate's NPS 81 advantage does not fully translate into omnichannel scores because the metric captures human service, not platform capability. Peers with lower NPS (estimated 60–70 range) may have more sophisticated servicing platforms, reflecting a classic community bank trade-off: relationship quality versus digital infrastructure.
: Personalization & Client Intelligence Score 2.68 / 5.0 | Peer: 2 | Gap: +0.68 | level 3 Established
What We See: NPS 81 World Class for 15 consecutive quarters [E-0073] is the highest-confidence evidence item for: it demonstrates personalized client outcomes at sustained scale. CEO Sowers Q1 2026: 'the majority of our new business continues to come from referrals' [E-0119] — the referral-dominant acquisition model is the behavioral output of successful personalization. Revolving lines of credit CAGR 16% [E-0078] indicates RM-driven cross-sell effectiveness. CalPrivate serves HNW clients, legal industry professionals, and closely-held businesses [E-0078] with a 'RM-memory' personalization model: relationship managers carry client knowledge that substitutes for platform-based personalization. Customer Intelligence is capped at level 3 (ISS-002) due to CRM fragmentation.
Why It Matters: 's +0.68 peer gap is the bank's most pronounced above-peer advantage in Pillar 2 — but it is also the most fragile, because it is human-capital-dependent. When a long-tenured RM departs, their client knowledge departs with them unless systematized in a CRM. FSC converts RM memory into platform memory: household management, financial accounts 360, relationship history, and next-best-action all preserve relationship context across RM transitions. The advantage becomes durable only when it is encoded in the platform.
Peer Context: score 2.68 vs peer median 2.00 (+0.68). Second-largest positive gap after. CalPrivate's personalization advantage is the most distinctive commercial signal in the assessment: a community bank delivering NPS 81 across 15 quarters through pure relationship management excellence. Peers (BMRC, RBB, BCAL) are estimated at 2.0, reflecting average community bank personalization capability.
per_pillar_md.P3:
P3 is CalPrivate Bank's highest-scoring pillar and its most durable competitive advantage. The combination of zero enforcement actions, CRA High Satisfactory under Large Institution procedures, Board-certified compliance expertise, and an active BCP/DR posture places CalPrivate in the top tier of SV1 peers on operational and compliance maturity. this area also sets the foundational conditions under which every Zennify technology recommendation can be deployed with confidence.
: Process Automation Score 2.81 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.31 | level 3 Established
What We See: Power Automate confirmed in production for workflow automation [E-0094] — a direct Microsoft 365 integration capability. nCino (Q1 2023) has automated key aspects of commercial lending origination: lead-to-close tracking, document generation, approval workflows [E-0105]. Centrix Positive Pay provides automated fraud prevention for commercial accounts [E-0085]. Treasury One handles treasury and payments automation [E-0085]. ServiceNow (ITSM) confirmed for internal IT ticket management and service workflows [E-0094]. COO Pierron — 25 years of banking operations and payments, 7 years EVP Head of Payments [E-0119] — leads an active operational efficiency mandate. subcaps score 2.5–3.5: workflow automation (3.0) and RPA/process automation (3.0) strong; cross-system automation limited by integration debt.
Why It Matters: Power Automate's presence is the most important signal: CalPrivate can build and deploy automated workflows within the Microsoft ecosystem. The constraint is that Power Automate cannot reach beyond M365 — nCino data, IFS Banking data, and FIS data are outside its scope without an API layer. MuleSoft (R-002) removes this constraint: once an integration layer is in place, Power Automate can trigger cross-system workflows (nCino loan event → FIS core booking → FSC case creation → Treasury One notification) that are currently manual. 's path to level 4 Advanced runs through MuleSoft.
Peer Context: score 2.81 vs peer median 2.50 (+0.31). Above peers. Power Automate + nCino workflow automation + ServiceNow ITSM represents a more mature automation stack than most SV1 $1B–$5B community banks, where automation often means spreadsheet macros or basic rule-based systems.
: Operational Risk & Fraud Score 2.63 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.13 | level 3 Established
What We See: Centrix Positive Pay deployed for commercial fraud detection and check payment protection [E-0085]. BSA/AML department confirmed with dedicated VP-level AML officer [E-0085]. CCO Meitzen (ex-OCC examiner, BSA/AML expertise, Aug 2025 appointment) [E-0019] and Director Lonowski (ex-FDIC San Francisco Regional Director) [E-0095] provide dual regulatory expertise for risk oversight. CECL allowance for credit losses model in quarterly production [E-0106]. ISS-001 MATERIAL: NPA ratio deteriorated from 0.47% (Q4 2024) to 2.00% (Q4 2025), triggering an level 3 ceiling on. Q1 2026: CEO Sowers — 'laser focused on reducing criticized, classified and non-performing assets. We believe reserves are adequate' [E-0119]. Credit metrics described as 'improving over prior quarter' by Q1 2026.
Why It Matters: The ISS-001 credit quality cap is the only MATERIAL issue with an active Q1 2026 improvement trajectory. This is important context: the level 3 ceiling on is not a structural deficiency but a temporary constraint reflecting a credit cycle correction actively being remediated. The CECL model in production (quarterly update cycles, formal governance) [E-0106] and the nCino portfolio analytics opportunity (R-004) provide the mechanism for accelerating credit recovery — unified credit data feeds more accurate risk models, and better models support faster identification of deteriorating credits.
Peer Context: score 2.63 vs peer median 2.50 (+0.13). Above peers despite ISS-001 cap. CalPrivate's Centrix Positive Pay + BSA/AML + ex-OCC CCO combination is stronger than the estimated peer baseline, even with the credit quality ceiling applied.
: Compliance & CRA Score 3.07 / 5.0 | Peer: 3 | Gap: +0.07 | level 3 Established
What We See: FDIC CRA examination (March 2024): High Satisfactory rating across all three performance tests (Lending, Investment, Services), rated under Large Institution CRA examination procedures [E-0090]. Zero enforcement actions confirmed across FDIC, OCC, CFPB, and California DFPI databases [E-0024]. BSA/AML department with dedicated VP-level officer [E-0085]. CCO Andrew Meitzen: ex-OCC examiner, enterprise risk, BSA/AML [E-0019]. Board Director Kathy Lonowski: ex-FDIC San Francisco Regional Director, supervised 350+ FIs with $1T AUM combined [E-0095]. CDARS and ICS (Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service / Insured Cash Sweep) deployed for large deposit insurance optimization [E-0096]. SBA Preferred Lender; Community Bank SBA 504 Lender of the Year [E-0124]. October 2025 Privacy Notice updated for CCPA/CPRA compliance [E-0097]. subcaps score 3.0–3.5 — the second-highest category average in the entire assessment.
Why It Matters: = 3.07 is tied with as the highest category score in the assessment. It reflects genuine, documented compliance depth: not a claim, but a formal FDIC examination outcome under the most rigorous applicable testing regime. This posture has direct implications for every Zennify technology recommendation. Banks with active enforcement actions face technology adoption constraints; CalPrivate has none. The ex-OCC CCO and ex-FDIC board director represent a dual-layer compliance review framework that can evaluate and approve Salesforce FSC data architecture, MuleSoft API governance, and Einstein AI model risk management with institutional credibility. Compliance is the enabler, not the gatekeeper.
Peer Context: score 3.07 vs peer median 3.00 (+0.07). CalPrivate is at or above peers on compliance — notable because HAFC (Hanmi Financial, $7.6B, NASDAQ-listed) has larger compliance investment capacity. CalPrivate's outperformance on a per-asset basis confirms that compliance maturity is an institutional value, not merely a scale outcome.
: Business Resilience & TPRM Score 2.84 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.34 | level 3 Established
What We See: CTO Birkmann holds BCP/DR certifications; FlexPod Cisco UCS + NetApp architecture designed for disaster recovery and high availability [E-0093]. BCP is 'tested annually' per bank communications. CalPrivate provided banking services to wildfire-affected clients (LA area wildfires) in early 2025 — demonstrating activated crisis response capability [E-0114]. CDARS/ICS deployment provides deposit insurance resilience for large depositors [E-0096]. 100+ technology project portfolio under CTO Birkmann [E-0093] provides vendor management discipline. Third-party risk management (TPRM) capability is demonstrated through 13 confirmed vendor platforms operating with formal governance relationships. subcaps score in the 3.0–3.5 range.
Why It Matters: Business Resilience is the second-strongest category in Pillar 3. The wildfire banking response [E-0114] is the most compelling evidence: it is one thing to test a BCP annually; it is another to activate it for a real-world crisis and maintain client service continuity. This resilience posture is directly relevant to the Salesforce recommendation set: FlexPod's existing high-availability architecture provides the on-premises foundation for a hybrid cloud deployment (Azure + FlexPod) that MuleSoft and Data Cloud require. The infrastructure resilience is already built; the application layer is what needs completion.
Peer Context: score 2.84 vs peer median 2.50 (+0.34). Third-largest positive gap in the assessment. CalPrivate's BCP/DR certifications + wildfire response activation + FlexPod architecture represent above-peer operational resilience. Most SV1 $1B–$5B community banks do not have documented crisis activation events; CalPrivate's wildfire response is a differentiated proof point.
per_pillar_md.P4:
P4 is CalPrivate Bank's lowest-scoring pillar and the primary opportunity horizon for the Zennify engagement. this area reflects a fundamental pattern: technology investment is present and documented, but architectural coherence is absent. Thirteen confirmed vendor platforms operate without a unified integration or data layer. The board AI mandate [E-0002] and COO AI automation mandate [E-0085] exist in the presence of a Analytics & AI score of 2.09 — the gap between aspiration and architecture is the opportunity.
: Data Management & Governance Score 2.21 / 5.0 | Peer: 2 | Gap: +0.21 | level 2 Developing
What We See: CECL allowance for credit losses model in quarterly production with formal governance — the most significant positive signal [E-0106]. SVP Credit Risk Analytics role (May 2026) requires Python, R, ML, CECL, Moody's Analytics, nCino, and PrecisionLender [E-0085] — confirming enterprise data warehouse construction is actively beginning. Privacy governance: CCPA/CPRA-compliant Privacy Notice updated October 2025 [E-0097]. Confirmed data platforms: D365, nCino, IFS Banking, FIS RDC, Treasury One — all independent data silos [E-0085, E-0120]. No CDP, no named MDM platform, no enterprise data warehouse confirmed. capability range: 1.5–3.0. Best capability: Privacy Governance (3.0). Weakest capability cluster: MDM subcaps (– = 1.5 — the lowest evidence-supported scores in the full 698-capability assessment).
Why It Matters: The MDM score of 1.5 is the most diagnostically precise finding in the P4 assessment. CalPrivate has a customer in D365 (loan cycle), a borrower in nCino, an account holder in IFS Banking, a depositor in FIS, and a treasury client in Treasury One — with no reconciliation layer between these five records. The SVP Credit Risk Analytics role requirement to 'ensure quality, availability, and integrity of loan/credit risk data across platforms and business units' [E-0085] confirms that management already recognizes this fragmentation as a priority. Data Cloud resolves the MDM gap by treating all five platform records as data sources feeding one unified profile — with identity resolution, calculated insights, and activation capabilities.
Peer Context: score 2.21 vs peer median 2.00 (+0.21). CalPrivate is above peers, but both are in level 2 Developing territory. Data management is the developing frontier for the entire SV1 $1B–$5B cohort — no peer is confirmed to have a CDP or MDM platform at this tier.
: Analytics & AI Enablement Score 2.09 / 5.0 | Peer: 2 | Gap: +0.09 | level 2 Developing
What We See: CECL ML model in quarterly production: the bank runs a formal machine learning model with quarterly update cycles, formal governance, and regulated output disclosure [E-0106]. This is the highest-evidence AI signal in the entire P4 assessment ( = 3.0). Power BI inferred from M365 stack [E-0094]. Chairman Isakow Q4 2025: AI investment named explicitly [E-0002]. COO Pierron AI-driven automation mandate [E-0085]. SVP Credit Risk Analytics requires Python/R/ML [E-0085]. capability range: 1.0–3.0. Top: Data Science (3.0). Weakest: AI Agents (1.0 — not deployed). Analytics Data Platform (1.5) — no enterprise analytics platform confirmed.
Why It Matters: The gap between the dual AI mandate (board + COO) and the score of 2.09 is the most consequential finding for the Zennify sales conversation. CalPrivate wants to do AI; it has demonstrated it can govern ML (CECL); it does not yet have the data infrastructure to scale AI beyond CECL. Einstein AI and Agentforce (R-007) build on top of the Data Cloud unified profile — which builds on top of MuleSoft ingestion pipelines — which builds on top of FSC as the primary activation target. The AI capability CalPrivate's Chairman and COO have mandated is three infrastructure layers away from becoming real. Each Zennify recommendation in Phase 1 and Phase 2 is a prerequisite for Phase 3 AI outcomes.
Peer Context: score 2.09 vs peer median 2.00 (+0.09). CalPrivate is marginally above the SV1 peer median on analytics and AI, driven by the CECL model. Both CalPrivate and peers are in early level 2 territory on this category — the entire $1B–$5B community bank cohort is at the threshold of AI adoption.
: Technology Architecture Score 2.54 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.04 | level 3 Established
What We See: FlexPod Cisco UCS + NetApp deployed as primary infrastructure platform with confirmed BCP/DR capability [E-0093]. ServiceNow ITSM confirmed for service management and IT operations [E-0094]. Microsoft 365 full suite (SharePoint Online, Teams, Power Apps, Power Automate, Outlook) [E-0094]. Active Directory for identity and access management. CIO Hurtik implemented SDLC/SCRUM methodology; LeSS (Large-Scale Scrum) and Change Control Board referenced [E-0094]. Architecture strategy documented in IR decks: 'create frictionless client experience through integrations of core, origination, servicing and online banking platforms' [E-0107]. Integration Architecture = 2.0 (capped level 4 per ISS-005: 7+ vendors without iPaaS).
Why It Matters: The technology architecture has all the components of a mature hybrid cloud infrastructure — FlexPod for compute, Azure (strongly inferred) for cloud services, M365 for productivity, ServiceNow for ITSM — but no integration layer connecting the application portfolio. The CTO's stated architecture principle [E-0107] of frictionless integration is aspirational without MuleSoft: each vendor integration is currently custom-built. This creates technical debt at exactly the point when CalPrivate is adding its most significant systems (nCino 2023, COO operational systems 2026). MuleSoft's API-led connectivity model converts custom integrations into reusable system, process, and experience layers — the architectural discipline the CTO's stated principle requires.
Peer Context: score 2.54 vs peer median 2.50 (+0.04). At peer median. CalPrivate's FlexPod + M365 + ServiceNow stack is comparable to or slightly above SV1 peer infrastructure maturity. The integration deficit is a shared SV1 challenge — most community banks at this tier have custom point-to-point integrations rather than enterprise iPaaS.
: Cybersecurity Score 2.67 / 5.0 | Peer: 2.5 | Gap: +0.17 | level 3 Established
What We See: Annual Report cybersecurity investment: CIO Hurtik stated 'the board investment in cybersecurity allows me to sleep at night' [E-0094]. SANS cybersecurity training certifications held by CTO Birkmann [E-0093]. IT Management Committee focus on 'enhancing focus on cybersecurity and emerging security trends' [E-0107]. CIO Hurtik's background: Trace 3 (cybersecurity consulting) and Active Directory implementation [E-0094]. Microsoft 365 Defender and Azure AD (Entra ID) inferred from M365 deployment [E-0094].
